texts.title: A Vote for a Vote
texts.body: {senator.name} of {senator.house} has a motion before the Senate this session, and has come to count heads. They want your vote. They do not offer money for it. They offer a vote of their own: give your word, and {senator.house} owes your house a vote. It votes for the next motion your house moves, whichever way it leans, unless that motion strikes at it. Your vote on theirs is declared for it, and is still yours to change until the Senate sits; but a word given and not kept is written down, and {senator.house} takes no word of yours on a vote for eight years.

choices.give_your_word: Give your word, and take theirs. Vote for their motion, or they will remember it.
choices.name_a_price: Tell them a vote costs more than a vote, and sell them yours for their motion.
choices.keep_your_vote: Tell them your vote is your own.

texts.title: A Bought Vote Called In
texts.body: {buyer.name} of {buyer.house} has another motion before the Senate. They paid for your vote once, and they have not forgotten it. They do not mean to pay again. A house that sells its vote once, they say, has told the chamber what it is, and they are sure you would not want the chamber reminded. The vote itself is cast in the chamber, as always, and they will be watching how you cast it.

choices.vote_as_they_ask: Say you will vote for it. Vote otherwise, and they will remember it.
choices.give_back_the_coin: Send back what they paid, and more, and be done with them.
choices.show_them_the_door: Tell them the bargain was for one vote.

texts.title: The Vote Still Undecided
texts.body: Your motion comes to the vote at the end of the session, and {doubter.name} of {doubter.house} has not said which way their house will go. They lean neither for it nor against. In a close count that is the vote that decides it. A head who thinks well enough of you leans your way, and {doubter.name} is not far off it.

choices.make_your_case: Go and make your case to them in person (1 influence). It may be enough to bring them over.
choices.have_them_to_dinner: Have them to dinner, and talk of anything but the motion (400 credits). It is the likeliest to bring them over.
choices.speak_from_the_floor: Speak for it from the floor, and let them hear it there. It may bring them over, if they were nearly there.
choices.leave_them_be: Leave them to make up their own mind.

texts.title: The Empty Seat on the Bench
texts.body: When the vote was called, your house did not vote. {leader.name} of {leader.house}, who leads your bench, voted, and looked along the bench to see who had not. A house that sits on a bench and will not stand up with it is talked about on the bench before it is talked about anywhere else.

choices.it_was_conscience: Say you could not vote for it, and would not vote against your friends.
choices.say_it_will_not_happen_again: Say it will not happen again.
choices.send_a_gift: Send a gift to their house, and no letter with it.
choices.your_vote_is_your_own: Say your vote is your own to cast or keep.

texts.title: A Feast for the Ayes
texts.body: Your motion carried. The houses that carried it expect to be thanked, and in the Reach that is done at a table. {ally.name} of {ally.house}, who voted with you, has asked whose table it will be.

choices.your_table: Give the dinner yourself, and seat {ally.name} at your right hand.
choices.their_table: Let {ally.name} give it, and go as their guest. The city will say it was their motion.
choices.a_letter: Thank them by letter, and keep your evening for yourself.

texts.title: The House That Voted Against You
texts.body: Your motion carried, and {loser.name} of {loser.house} voted against it to the end. They have lost in front of the whole chamber, and {loser.house} remembers who it lost to.

choices.offer_them_something: Go to them and offer them something for their trouble.
choices.let_them_lose: Let them lose. It is what a vote is.

texts.title: An Old Grudge Moves a Motion
texts.body: There is a motion before the Senate against your house, and it is {rival.name} of {rival.house} who moved it. Nobody in the chamber is surprised. They have held a grudge against your house since the chamber last saw them come off worse against you, and they have been waiting.

choices.answer_them_on_the_floor: Answer them on the floor, and name the old quarrel.
choices.make_your_peace: Go to them and make your peace. It will not stop this vote.

texts.title: An Old Grudge Against Your Motion
texts.body: Your motion comes to the vote this session, and {rival.name} of {rival.house} is speaking against it in every corridor of the Senate. It is not the motion they mind. They have held a grudge against your house since the chamber last saw them come off worse against you, and this is the first chance they have had to make you pay for it. A head who thinks ill enough of you leans against what you move, and {rival.name} does.

choices.buy_them_off: Send them something to let it go (600 credits). They may think well enough of you again not to lean against it.
choices.answer_them_on_the_floor: Answer them on the floor, and name the old quarrel. They will still lean against it; the chamber will think the better of you.
choices.let_it_cost_you: Let them talk. Their house leans against your motion, and the grudge is spent on it.

texts.title: The Senate's Act Falls on a Friend
texts.body: An Act of the Senate has carried, against the votes of {friend.house}. {friend.name} fought it to the last, and has written to you: not to complain, they say, but because a friend should hear it from them first. They would like to know what you mean to do. An Act is undone as it was made: by another Act, moved in the Senate.

choices.promise_the_repeal: Promise to move its repeal when the chamber will hear it.
choices.help_them_through: Send them help to carry it through the year, and ask nothing.
choices.the_law_is_the_law: Tell them the law is the law, for your house as for theirs.

texts.title: A Purse on the Senate Floor
texts.body: On the floor today it came out that you paid {bought.house} for its vote. The vote is struck, and the chamber thinks the less of your house. {bought.name} is the one who had to walk out past everyone, and is waiting to hear what you will say.

choices.take_it_on_yourself: Say before the chamber that it was your doing, not theirs.
choices.make_it_good: Pay them for what it has cost them.

texts.title: One of Yours Stands for Office
texts.body: {kin.name} has put their name down for office at the coming count. They have not asked your leave, and they do not need it: it is their name. The house can speak for them at the count, or pay for a canvass, as it can for anyone of the house who stands. What they have come to ask is what you will do yourself.

choices.walk_the_wards: Walk the wards with them, so the city sees the house behind them.
choices.teach_them_the_floor: Teach them how a crowd is won.
choices.let_them_win_it: Tell them an office is won by the one who stands.

texts.title: A Smear After the Election
texts.body: {accuser.name} of {accuser.house} lost at the count to one of your house, and is saying in every square that the count was bought. It was not, or not more than any count is. But it is being said, and the squares like to hear it.

choices.open_the_accounts: Open the house's accounts to the praetors.
choices.answer_in_kind: Pay a pamphleteer to say what is known of their own canvass.

texts.title: The Pamphlet Scandal
texts.body: Your pamphleteer and the one {accuser.name} of {accuser.house} pays have been at it all year. The squares have enjoyed it. Nobody believes either side, which is to say that both houses are now believed to have bought what votes they could. {accuser.name} has sent word that they will stop if you will.

choices.call_off_your_writer: Call off your writer. The squares will say your house blinked first.
choices.before_a_praetor: Have their pamphlets brought before a praetor.
choices.let_the_writers_write: Let the writers write. {accuser.house} will come out of it no better than yours.

texts.title: The One Who Won the Office
texts.body: {victor.name} of {victor.house} took the office {kin.name} stood for. The count is posted on the Senate doors. {kin.name} wants to know whether the house will ask for it to be read again, and so do your people.

choices.congratulate_them: Go and congratulate them where the city can see. {kin.name} will see it too.
choices.demand_a_recount: Demand the count be read again. {kin.name} will know the house fought for them, and the squares will doubt the count.

texts.title: A Riot on the Day of the Count
texts.body: The squares do not believe the magistrates this year, and they did not believe the count. By noon there were stones at the booths and a crowd at the Senate doors, and the lictors have sent to every house to ask what it will do.

choices.keep_the_peace: Send your house's people to keep the peace at the booths. The commons will see who came.
choices.speak_from_the_steps: Speak to the crowd from the Senate steps. The squares may believe the count again.
choices.call_the_lictors: Tell the lictors to clear the squares. The magistrates will thank you; the commons will not.
choices.bar_the_doors: Bar your doors until it is over. The commons will see whose doors were shut.

texts.title: The Consul-Elect's Feast
texts.body: The count is done, and {grandee.name} of {grandee.house} is Senior Consul for ten years: they will preside, speak from the chair, break a tied Senate, and once in their term strike a motion with a veto. Tonight they dine the Senate. Everyone who means to have anything of the consuls in those ten years will be at that table, and everyone will see who is not.

choices.go_and_be_seen: Go, and be seen to go. A consul remembers who came to their table.
choices.send_a_gift_ahead: Send a gift ahead of you that the table will talk about. A consul remembers who came to their table.
choices.ask_for_your_bench: Go, and ask across the table what the consulship will do for your bench. It will not be liked.

texts.title: Your Colleague, the Consul
texts.body: You and {grandee.name} of {grandee.house} hold the two chairs of the consulship. Each of you can strike the other's business with a veto: once in the term, {grandee.name} will strike the first motion of yours that strikes at their house, at their bench's leader or at their bench's line, and the chamber is waiting to see which of you will try it first. {grandee.name} has asked to see you before the first session.

choices.divide_the_year: Divide the consulship's business between you: neither of you strikes the other's.
choices.the_senior_chair_leads: Tell them the senior chair leads.
choices.keep_your_counsel: Keep your own counsel, and watch them. You will learn how they work.
